stimulus.title: Clay on two turntables
stimulus.text: Two turntables have the same mass M and the same radius R, and each turns freely on a frictionless vertical axle. Turntable A is a uniform solid disk (IA = ½MR², given). Turntable B is a ring with nearly all its mass at the rim (IB = MR², given). Both spin at the same angular velocity ω₀. A small lump of clay of mass m is dropped straight down onto each turntable and sticks at its rim. Model the clay as a point object.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: After the clay sticks, which turntable spins faster, or do they spin at the same rate? Justify your answer without using equations.

rubric.point: Claims turntable B (the ring) spins faster after the clay sticks
accept: B ends with the larger angular velocity

rubric.point: Reason: B starts with more angular momentum (larger rotational inertia at the same ω₀), and the same clay at the same radius adds the same rotational inertia, which is a smaller fraction of B’s total, so B’s angular velocity drops by a smaller fraction
accept: the clay is a smaller share of B’s rotational inertia
B has more angular momentum to share with the same clay

parts.sample: Turntable B spins faster. Both spin at the same rate, but B’s mass is farther from the axle, so B has the larger rotational inertia and more angular momentum. The clay adds the same extra rotational inertia to each (same mass, same radius). That extra inertia is a smaller fraction of B’s total, so B slows by a smaller fraction, and it ends up turning faster.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A turntable has rotational inertia I = βMR², where β is a number that depends on its shape. Derive an expression for its angular velocity ω after the clay sticks, in terms of β, M, m and ω₀. Begin your derivation by writing a fundamental physics principle or an equation from the reference information.

rubric.point: Uses conservation of angular momentum for the turntable-clay system, with the condition (no net external torque about the axle: the axle is frictionless and the clay falls straight down, so it brings no angular momentum about the axle)
accept: L_i = L_f because the net external torque about the axle is zero

rubric.point: Writes I_f = βMR² + mR² with the clay’s initial angular momentum about the axle equal to zero

parts.sample: System: turntable and clay. The axle is frictionless, and the clay falls straight down, parallel to the axle, so it brings no angular momentum about the axle; gravity and the forces during the landing are vertical and exert no torque about the vertical axle. The net external torque about the axle is zero, so L is constant. Before: L = βMR²ω₀. After: I = βMR² + mR². βMR²ω₀ = (βMR² + mR²)ω, so ω = βMω₀/(βM + m).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain how your expression from part (b) supports or contradicts your answer to part (a).

rubric.point: Reads the dependence: ω = ω₀/(1 + m/(βM)), so a larger β gives a smaller m/(βM) and a larger final ω (closer to ω₀)
Applies it: β = ½ for A and β = 1 for B, so ω_B > ω_A (e.g. ω_A = ω₀/(1 + 2m/M), ω_B = ω₀/(1 + m/M))
States that this agrees with the claim in part (a) that B spins faster

parts.sample: Rewrite the result as ω = ω₀/(1 + m/(βM)). A larger β makes m/(βM) smaller, so the denominator is closer to 1 and ω is closer to ω₀. Turntable A has β = ½: ω_A = ω₀/(1 + 2m/M). Turntable B has β = 1: ω_B = ω₀/(1 + m/M), which is larger. So B ends up spinning faster, which supports the claim in part (a).
